transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Elisa Moreno (CTO, Aerilon), Tom Anders (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Head of Security), Jules Kwan (Product)

Summary: quick discovery then deep dive on model choices for POC, benchmarks and timelines. A lot of focus on multilingual quality and throughput.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Chen from Redwood, and with me is Raj our SE. how's everyone?
[00:08] Elisa: hi Maya, thanks, yes all good. we're excited to scope the POC.
[00:12] Tom: hey, yeah, we want to validate open models before committing to a hosted provider; latency and cost are big for us.
[00:20] Raj: cool, great. quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, recommended models and quantization, benchmark plan, and security checklist. feel free to interrupt.
[00:28] Jules: sounds good.

[02:05] Maya: Elisa, maybe start with the high-level success criteria for the POC so we can map models to goals?
[02:12] Elisa: sure. primary use case is document extraction and summarization across product manuals in english, spanish, and german. success looks like: 1) extraction accuracy > 88% on our validation set, 2) p95 latency under 600ms for single doc summarization, 3) cost per doc less than $0.05 at our expected scale.
[02:35] Tom: to add, we need throughput of about 12 qps for the peak window, average doc length 1.2k tokens, and some long docs up to 8k tokens run as chunked flows.
[02:50] Raj: good - that's helpful. when you say accuracy, is that exact span extraction F1 or end-to-end QA?
[02:57] Elisa: mostly F1 on labelled spans, but we will also judge summaries with a small human eval.

[05:10] Priya: on security - we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. we also have data residency concerns for eu users.
[05:25] Maya: totally understandable. Redwood has SOC 2, we support SAML SSO and integrations with customer KMS for private deployments. we can pull the SOC2 report and our architecture notes.
[05:37] Raj: for private deployment we can discuss VPC-connected control plane or on-prem package; for POC we usually run in a dedicated tenant with KMS integration, depending on customer preference.

[07:00] Tom: okay on models - what are you recommending for open-model shortlist? we've been experimenting with a few but haven't standardized.
[07:07] Raj: from our POV for this workload (extraction + summarization, multilingual), shortlist usually: Llama 3 13B (or llm- variants), Mistral 7B/ mixing 8x? (note: some transcription), Falcon 40B-instruct quantized, Mixtral 8x (we'll clarify), and a fine-tune/light-adapter on top of Llama 3. also consider smaller Mistral for faster throughput if quality accepts tradeoffs.
[07:40] Maya: i'll say explicitly: Llama 3 family gives strong quality for instruction tasks; Mistral 7/8 variants are competitive and often cheaper/ faster when quantized; Falcon 40B sometimes wins on certain summarization metrics but costs more to run.
[08:02] Elisa: what about multilingual? Spanish is fine but german has been tougher for us, especially with domain jargon.
[08:10] Raj: Llama 3 has decent multilingual coverage; Mistral models sometimes need adapter layers or LoRA for domain + language. we recommend baseline runs with off-the-shelf models, then a small adapter fine-tune on 1-5k in-domain pairs for German.

[09:15] Tom: latency - can we hit p95 < 600ms for 1.2k tokens?
[09:20] Raj: with batching and right GPU sizes, yes for smaller models; for 13B Llama 3 on a T4-class or better tuned for inference and 16-32 token prompt it should be ok; larger models like Falcon 40B will need A10/A100 and may increase cost. quantization (4-bit) plus Redwood's continuous batching and KV cache pruning help.
[09:43] Maya: note that latency targets depend on whether you want single-request low-latency or you can accept micro-batching. you said 12 qps peak, that can be handled with dedicated instances and autoscale.

[11:50] Jules: for benchmarks, what metrics do you propose we run?
[11:55] Raj: we typically measure: quality (F1 for extraction, rouge/bertscore for summarization), latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec and qps), cost per 1k tokens, and memory usage. we also run edge cases - long docs chunking behavior and failure modes.
[12:20] Tom: can Redwood run the benchmark or do we need to run it in our infra?
[12:25] Maya: we can run both. for initial runs we often run in Redwood test env with your sample data (redacted if needed). if you prefer to validate in your VPC/private deployment we can provide a test harness and small runner.

[14:00] Elisa: timeline - we want results in two weeks ideally. is that realistic?
[14:05] Raj: two weeks to get baseline numbers yes: 1-2 days to receive samples, 2-3 days to set up runs and sizing, then runs and analysis ~3-5 days. so baseline in ~10 business days. added adapter fine-tune would be extra week.
[14:30] Tom: great. what about cost numbers - ballpark for baseline?
[14:35] Maya: for off-the-shelf Llama 3 13B quantized, expect $0.01-0.03 per doc depending on batching and doc size; Falcon 40B could be 3-4x. we'll provide a spreadsheet with cost sensitivity to batch size and seq length.

[16:12] Priya: compliance - we need the SOC2 report and pen test summary; also, is there a way to have audit logs shipped to our Splunk?
[16:20] Maya: yes, we can forward logs to Splunk or S3. we'll attach SOC2 and our security architecture.

[18:00] Raj: about model ops - version pinning, rollbacks, and auto-fallback: Redwood supports pinning model versions and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency SLO breached; we can configure canary and A/B.
[18:20] Tom: good. for evaluation, we'll provide a small labeled set for extraction (500 examples) and a set for human eval for summary quality.

[20:00] Maya: any hard blockers?
[20:05] Priya: only if we can't integrate KMS or if logs can't be forwarded. otherwise fine.

[22:30] Raj: on sizing - given 12 qps peak and 1.2k avg tokens, our preliminary suggestion: start with 2 dedicated 80GB A10-like instances for baseline testing with autoscale policy, or 4x smaller 48GB instances if you need cheaper ops and can micro-batch. Raj: we'll include exact VM/GPU SKUs in the follow-up.

[25:00] Jules: curious on quantization - are 4-bit models stable for extraction tasks? we've had hallucination increase in earlier tests.
[25:08] Raj: yes some increases possible. tradeoff: 4-bit gives big cost savings, often minimal quality drop for classification/extraction, but for domain-specific jargon sometimes 8-bit outperforms 4-bit. we recommend a head-to-head test in the POC.

[27:40] Elisa: ok. what about multilingual fine-tuning cost/time?
[27:45] Raj: small adapter tuning (LoRA) on 1-5k steps is pretty quick - a day or two on a single 80GB GPU, cheap-ish. full fine-tune larger footprint. we usually do LoRA for POC.

[30:00] Tom: can you list the shortlisted models again with rationale?
[30:07] Raj: sure: Llama 3 13B - best general instruction quality and multilingual baseline; Mistral 7B/8x - faster cheaper, good with adapters; Falcon 40B-instruct - strong summarization in some tests but heavier; Llama 3 7B (smaller) - for throughput if quality OK; plus a small custom LoRA on top of Llama 3 for german domain-specific terms.

[33:10] Maya: we'll also recommend quantization profiles: q4f32 / q8_0 depending on hardware and acceptable quality delta. we'll attach recommended configs.

[35:40] Elisa: final ask - can you provide a sample benchmark plan doc? we'll want to see specifics: dataset splits, metrics thresholds, and run scripts.
[35:50] Maya: yes - action: we'll send benchmark template and runbook. Raj will include model config + expected costs.

[38:00] Priya: one more question, retention: we need data not retained beyond 30 days for POC and logs forwarded - is that doable?
[38:08] Maya: yes, POC short retention window is standard; we can set 30-day retention and disable logging of raw inputs where required.

[40:20] Tom: ok looks good. any competitors or procurement constraints?
[40:25] Elisa: we have procurement evaluating OpenAI for hosted plus internal infra; security is leaning towards vendor that supports KMS.
[40:35] Maya: understood. we'll provide everything for the security review.

[42:00] Jules: recap?
[42:05] Maya: recap: 1) Redwood sends benchmark template, model shortlist, and sizing guidance (Maya + Raj), 2) Aerilon shares sample dataset + target metrics (Tom), 3) Security docs/SOC2 (Maya) and security questionnaire answers (Priya), 4) schedule baseline runs week of Mar 15.
[42:25] Elisa: agree.
[42:30] Maya: i'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff. thanks everyone.
[42:36] Tom: thanks.
[42:40] Priya: thanks all.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional name and model variants mistranscribed in informal notes; we validated key model names in follow-up action items.
